title: Polynomial-Time Bounded Interpretation
statement: Let $f$ map Boolean words to Boolean words, and let $N$ assign a natural-number bound to each Boolean word. If $f$ is polynomial-time computable and the function sending $x$ to the unary word of length $N(x)$ is polynomial-time computable, then the function sending $x$ to the unary word whose length is the value of $f(x)$ when that value is at most $N(x)$, and zero otherwise, is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: The unary word of length $N(x)$ is polynomial-time computable as a function of $x$
replaced: If a binary-word producer and a unary bound producer are polynomial-time computable, then the unary word of the bounded value of the produced word is polynomial-time computable.
